why: The model crossing the engine boundary is protobuf-defined and generated into both
languages. The event stream crossing back is not. The engine encodes each event by
hand in packages/zig/wasm/src/abi.zig, and the TypeScript host declares a hand-written
union mirroring it in runner-adapter.ts. Two independent descriptions of one wire
format, with nothing holding them together — the same shape as every other pair in
this repository that has since been gated.
The failure it allows is quiet. A warning kind added on the engine side reaches the
host as a union member nothing handles: the `switch` has no arm for it, the warning is
dropped, and no test fails, because the host's type declares the kind does not exist.
An event kind added on the engine side is worse — `advanceZigRuntime` falls off the end
of its switch and returns undefined.
So every kind either side speaks is listed here. A kind in the engine and not in this
file fails the gate; so does one in this file that the host does not name.
This gates the vocabulary, not the payload. Whether the host reads every field of an
event it knows about is still the host's business and still untested here — the
conformance vectors in spec/conformance/host/ are where that lives.

events.why: The engine is asking the host to run a hook — prepare, publish or extend — and will not advance until resumed.
One action finished. Carries its compute root, next action ids, publish outcomes, and any warnings.
A route transition moved the run from one scene to another.
The run finished on its own.
The run stopped because the host cancelled it.
An extend hook returned a model that collides with the running one. The host raises it as ModelMergeError rather than a runtime fault, so it is read before the ok/error status is.

actionWarnings.why: A merge binding wrote to a STATE path the schema does not declare.
The run has no STATE schema, so writes were accepted without type checking. Carries every path written.
A next rule's condition binding is not a bool. Derived from NextRuleWarningKind, not a literal.
A next rule names a transition compute that carries no prog. Derived from NextRuleWarningKind, not a literal.

sceneWarnings.why: A next rule pointed at an action that already ran in this scene.

why: The needEffect envelope is hand-written on three sides, and until now two of them
were gated and the third was not. `events` above pins the kind, which is what
catches an event appearing on one side alone. It does not pin the fields, and the
fields are where this envelope actually moves: `bindings` was added to it because a
host had no way to know which bindings a multi-binding hook owed, and each side had
to be edited by hand.
The third side is the native host. It builds RequestJson field by field from
effect.Request, so a field added to the request reaches the WASM encoder and the
TypeScript host -- both under the `events` gate -- and is silently dropped by the
native host, with no compile error, because nothing requires the struct to be
complete. Two hosts would then hand a hook different envelopes for the same effect.
So the wire field names are listed here and every side must name all of them.

fields.name: id
fields.why: the effect the resume payload must answer

fields.name: role
fields.why: binding or extend; what the payload is for

fields.name: hook
fields.why: the hook name the host resolves

fields.name: sceneId
fields.why: the scene the effect fired in

fields.name: actionId
fields.why: the action the effect fired in

fields.name: callbackIndex
fields.why: which declared hook of the action this is

fields.name: binding
fields.why: the single binding, or null when the hook supplies several

fields.name: bindings
fields.why: every binding the hook is declared to supply

fields.name: contextJson
fields.why: the bindings already resolved, for the hook to read
